intent.raw_query: Portugal Algarve, $2200, beach holiday with wine tasting, September 2026 from London

experiences.name: Meia Praia Beach Day
experiences.description: Spend a relaxed afternoon at Meia Praia, one of the longest and most accessible beaches in the Algarve, located just minutes from Lagos town center. Since your flight arrives late on Day 1, plan this as a Day 2 morning-to-afternoon activity to ease into the trip. Rent a sun lounger, swim in calm Atlantic waters, and enjoy beachside snacks from nearby kiosks. Staying in Lagos ensures you can walk or take a short taxi to the beach without wasting time on long transfers.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine Tasting at Quinta dos Vales
experiences.description: Visit Quinta dos Vales, a renowned winery in the Algarve interior near Estômbar, just a 20-minute drive from Lagos or Portimão. Book an afternoon guided tour and tasting session sampling regional Algarve reds, whites, and rosés paired with local cheeses. Scheduling this mid-trip on a weekday afternoon avoids crowds and fits well after morning beach time. Staying in Portimão or Lagos keeps transfer times minimal and budget-friendly.

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Walk and Swim
experiences.description: Explore the dramatic golden limestone cliffs and crystal-clear coves of Praia da Marinha, consistently rated one of Europe's most beautiful beaches. Arrive in the morning to secure a spot before crowds build. The coastal walking trail connecting nearby coves is free and stunning. Base yourself in Lagoa or Carvoeiro to be within 10 minutes of this beach, avoiding the long drives that frustrated previous itineraries.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided kayak tour departing directly from Benagil Beach to paddle into the iconic Benagil Cave, a cathedral-like sea cave with a natural skylight. Tours depart in the morning when seas are calmest and light inside the cave is most dramatic. Book with a local operator based in Carvoeiro or Benagil to avoid long travel. This activity combines adventure, natural beauty, and coastal culture in one experience. Staying in Lagoa or Carvoeiro puts you within 5 minutes of the departure point.

experiences.name: Lagos Old Town Food and Wine Evening Walk
experiences.description: Join a small-group evening food and wine tour through the historic cobblestone streets of Lagos old town, sampling local Algarve wines, grilled sardines, cataplana seafood stew, and pastéis de nata at curated stops. This is ideal for Day 2 evening after your late Day 1 arrival, letting you settle in before diving into culture. Staying in Lagos means you walk out of your hotel door directly into the tour route, eliminating any transfer cost or time.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Faro Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage and arrange transfer to Lagoa Boutique Stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Lagoa Boutique Stay and freshen up. Take a leisurely stroll around Lagoa town centre, explore the local market square, and visit the Igreja Matriz de Lagoa (free entry). Pick up snacks and essentials at the nearby Pingo Doce supermarket to keep costs down.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into the area with a relaxed walk along Lagoa's main street. Enjoy your first taste of the Algarve at a local tasca (tavern).

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastel de nata at the airport or on arrival in Lagoa at a local café (~€2–3)
meals.lunch: Light snack from supermarket or café near the hotel (~€4–6)
meals.dinner: Tasca O Zé in Lagoa — traditional petiscos (Portuguese tapas) and grilled fish at budget prices (~€10–13 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Flight arrives at 13:00 so Day 1 is a short settling-in day. Buy a local SIM card at the airport for cheap data. Lagoa is centrally located in the Algarve, making it an excellent base for exploring both east and west.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia de Carvoeiro, one of the most scenic beaches near Lagoa (~10 min drive or local bus). Arrive early to claim a good spot on the golden sand. Swim, relax, and explore the dramatic limestone cliffs framing the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the cliffside boardwalk from Carvoeiro to the Algar Seco rock formations — a stunning natural sea cave and rock arch accessible for free. Bring water and sunscreen. Continue along the coastal path for panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa town for dinner. Browse the local wine shop to pick up an affordable bottle of Algarve wine (DOP Lagos or Lagoa region) to enjoy on the hotel terrace.

meals.breakfast: Café in Lagoa — galão (milky coffee) and toast with butter and jam (~€2–3)
meals.lunch: Snack bar at Carvoeiro beach — prego sandwich (beef roll) or bifana (~€5–7)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Castelo in Carvoeiro — fresh grilled sardines or cataplana (Portuguese seafood stew) (~€12–15)

day_by_day.notes: Bus 55 runs from Lagoa to Carvoeiro. Algar Seco is free and walkable from Carvoeiro beach. September weather is typically warm (24–28°C) with calm seas — ideal for swimming.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting morning: Visit Quinta dos Vales winery near Estômbar (15 min from Lagoa). This well-regarded Algarve estate offers affordable guided tastings and vineyard walks. Book in advance online for the best budget rate (~€10–15 for a tasting flight).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia da Marinha, consistently ranked one of Portugal's most beautiful beaches. Explore the hidden coves, sea arches, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Snorkelling is excellent here — bring your own gear or rent cheaply nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa for a quiet evening. Visit the local mercado (market) if open, or pick up regional cheeses, chouriço, and Algarve almonds for a budget picnic-style dinner on the hotel terrace.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria in Lagoa — croissant and coffee (~€2–3)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from supermarket — bread, local cheese, ham, fruit (~€4–5)
meals.dinner: Self-catered terrace dinner with local wine, regional cheeses, chouriço, olives, and almonds (~€8–10 total)

day_by_day.notes: Quinta dos Vales requires advance booking — check their website. Praia da Marinha has limited parking; arrive by midday. The beach has no facilities so bring everything you need.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves — the historic Moorish capital of the Algarve, just 15 min from Lagoa by train or bus. Visit the impressive red sandstone Castelo de Silves (€2.80 entry). Walk the ancient walls for panoramic views over the orange groves and river.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Silves old town: the Gothic cathedral (free), the Museu Arqueológico (€2 entry), and the charming cobblestone streets. Browse the local fruit and vegetable market near the river for cheap seasonal produce.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Silves before returning to Lagoa. Try the famous local orange-based desserts.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or local café in Lagoa (~€2–4)
meals.lunch: Café Ingles in Silves — set lunch menu (prato do dia) with soup, main, and drink (~€8–10)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves — renowned for affordable fresh seafood and regional dishes (~€13–16)

day_by_day.notes: Train from Tunes (near Lagoa) to Silves runs regularly and costs under €3 each way. Silves is very walkable. The castle is the highlight — allow at least 1.5 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Praia de Benagil — home to the world-famous Benagil Sea Cave (Algar de Benagil). Rent a kayak or SUP board from the beach (~€15–20/hr) to paddle into the cave independently, avoiding expensive boat tours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the coastal trail eastward from Benagil toward Praia do Carvalho — a hidden beach accessed via a tunnel through the cliff. Swim and relax in this secluded spot. Bring snacks as there are no facilities.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa. Visit a local adega (wine cellar) in Lagoa — the town is known for its wine production. Many small producers offer informal tastings for free or very low cost.

meals.breakfast: Café in Lagoa — coffee and tosta mista (toasted ham and cheese sandwich) (~€3–4)
meals.lunch: Snack bar at Benagil beach — grilled chicken sandwich or soup (~€5–7)
meals.dinner: A Tasca do Guloso in Lagoa — daily specials, hearty portions, very local crowd (~€9–12)

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Benagil early (before 10:00) to beat crowds. The cave is only accessible by water — kayaking is the most budget-friendly option. Check sea conditions before going.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip west to Lagos (40 min by train from Tunes). Start with Praia Dona Ana — a stunning sheltered beach with golden cliffs. Swim and explore the rock formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk into Lagos old town: visit the free Igreja de Santo António, the Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos, €3 entry), and the colourful mosaic-tiled streets. Stroll along the marina and the old city walls.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Lagos's vibrant but affordable nightlife scene. Many bars offer happy hour deals. Return to Lagoa by train (last train check required).

meals.lunch: O Camilo restaurant near Praia Dona Ana — try the percebes (barnacles) or fresh fish, set lunch menu (~€10–13)
meals.dinner: Adega da Marina in Lagos — traditional Portuguese cuisine, generous portions, great value (~€11–14)

day_by_day.notes: Train from Tunes to Lagos costs around €3.50 each way. Lagos is very walkable. Check the last return train time to Tunes to avoid being stranded.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge day. Sleep in and enjoy a slow morning at the hotel. Visit Lagoa's local market (held on Saturdays) for fresh produce, local honey, figs, and artisan goods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Praia de Porches — a quieter, less-touristy beach near Lagoa with calm waters and fewer crowds. Great for a peaceful afternoon swim and sunbathing.
day_by_day.evening: Wine tasting evening: Visit Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa — one of the oldest wine cooperatives in the Algarve, located right in Lagoa town. Affordable tasting sessions and bottles to take away (~€5–10).

meals.breakfast: Leisurely café breakfast in Lagoa — fresh bread, local butter, coffee (~€3–5)
meals.lunch: Market lunch — fresh fruit, local cheese, bread, and pastries from the morning market (~€5–7)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Boneca in Lagoa — local favourite, great grilled meats and fish, very affordable (~€10–13)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday market in Lagoa is a great budget opportunity to stock up on local produce. Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa is one of the best wine bargains in the region — their table wines start from €3 a bottle.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip east to Portimão and Praia da Rocha (20 min by bus or train). Start at Praia da Rocha — one of the Algarve's longest and most dramatic beaches with towering red-orange cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk into Portimão town. Visit the Museu de Portimão (free on Sundays, €3 other days) — an excellent museum about the city's sardine canning history. Browse the riverfront promenade and local shops.
day_by_day.evening: Portimão is famous for its grilled sardines — enjoy a riverside dinner before returning to Lagoa.

meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Praia da Rocha — piri-piri chicken wrap or fresh juice (~€6–8)
meals.dinner: Taberna da Maré in Portimão — legendary grilled sardines on the riverfront, extremely affordable (~€9–12)

day_by_day.notes: Bus 77 connects Lagoa to Portimão frequently. Praia da Rocha gets busy but is large enough to find space. The Portimão museum is one of the best free cultural experiences in the Algarve.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia de Armação de Pêra — a wide, long beach east of Lagoa with calm waters, popular with locals. Walk to the small whitewashed chapel of Nossa Senhora do Rochedo perched on the cliffs for great views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the inland village of Porches, famous for its traditional hand-painted azulejo (blue tile) pottery. Visit the Porches Pottery workshop — free to browse, affordable to buy small pieces as souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a cliffside bar near Carvoeiro. Many offer affordable happy hour deals with views over the Atlantic.

meals.lunch: Local restaurant in Armação de Pêra — prato do dia (daily special) with soup and main (~€8–10)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Leão in Lagoa — hearty Portuguese home cooking, great value menu (~€10–13)

day_by_day.notes: Porches Pottery is a great budget souvenir stop — small hand-painted tiles cost €5–10. Armação de Pêra is very popular with Portuguese families and offers a more authentic local beach experience.

day_by_day.morning: Wine and food pairing experience: Visit Quinta da Penina or another local estate near Mexilhoeira Grande for a morning wine tour and tasting. Focus on Algarve DOC wines — reds, whites, and the excellent local rosés (~€12–18 for a guided tasting).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia de Meia Praia near Lagos — a vast 4km stretch of calm, sheltered beach ideal for swimming. Less crowded than the rocky cove beaches, with warm shallow waters.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa. Cook a simple dinner using produce bought from the local market — fresh vegetables, local bread, and a bottle of Lagoa cooperative wine.

meals.lunch: Snack bar at Meia Praia beach — bifana or grilled chicken (~€5–7)
meals.dinner: Self-catered in hotel room or terrace — pasta with local chorizo, salad, bread, and Algarve wine (~€7–9 total)

day_by_day.notes: Meia Praia is accessible by train (Lagos station is a short walk away) or local bus. It is one of the calmest beaches in the western Algarve — ideal for families and relaxed swimming.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente — the southwestern tip of continental Europe (1 hr by bus from Lagoa via Portimão). Visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres (€3 entry) and walk the windswept cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 6km to Cabo de São Vicente lighthouse — the most southwesterly point of Europe. The views are breathtaking and entry to the grounds is free. Watch the famous Sagres sunset from the cape.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Sagres village before the return bus to Lagoa. Sagres has several affordable local restaurants catering to surfers and budget travellers.

meals.lunch: Café Sagres or packed lunch from supermarket at the cape (~€5–8)
meals.dinner: Restaurante A Tasca in Sagres — fresh tuna, grilled fish, and local wine at very reasonable prices (~€11–14)

day_by_day.notes: Bus from Portimão to Sagres takes about 1 hour and costs ~€5 each way. The walk between Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente is along a coastal path — wear good shoes. Check return bus times carefully.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach morning at Praia de Carvoeiro or Praia da Marinha — your choice of favourite beach from the trip. Swim, relax, and soak up the last of the Algarve sun.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lagoa for souvenir shopping and packing. Visit the local wine cooperative one last time to buy bottles of Algarve wine to take home (very affordable at €3–8 per bottle). Browse the local shops for almond sweets (Dom Rodrigos), carob products, and hand-painted ceramics.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Lagoa — splurge slightly on a cataplana (traditional Algarve seafood stew for two) at a local restaurant to celebrate the end of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Café in Lagoa — full Portuguese breakfast: eggs, toast, cheese, ham, coffee (~€4–6)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar — last grilled sardine sandwich by the sea (~€5–7)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Cacto in Lagoa — traditional cataplana de marisco (seafood stew), regional wine (~€15–18 as a treat)

day_by_day.notes: Buy wine at the cooperative in checked luggage-friendly quantities. Dom Rodrigos (almond and egg yolk sweets) are the iconic Algarve souvenir and cost around €6–8 per box. Carob chocolate is another great local product.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Lagoa. Enjoy a slow breakfast at a favourite café. Take a last walk around Lagoa town, visit the Igreja Matriz one more time, and say goodbye to the area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Lagoa Boutique Stay and arrange transfer to Faro Airport. Allow plenty of time for the ~45-minute journey. Spend any remaining euros on last-minute snacks or airport souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days of beaches, wine, fresh seafood, and Algarve sunshine.

meals.breakfast: Final café breakfast in Lagoa — pastel de nata, galão, and fresh orange juice (~€3–5)
meals.lunch: Airport café or packed snacks from supermarket (~€5–8)
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2 hours before your flight for check-in and security at Faro Airport. Taxis from Lagoa to Faro cost approximately €35–45; shared shuttle services are cheaper (~€15–20 per person). Book in advance.

trip_options.title: Classic Portugal Algarve Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Faro Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Lagoa Boutique Stay (~35 min drive). Check in, freshen up, and settle into your room.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation stroll around Lagoa town center. Visit the charming Igreja Matriz de Lagoa (parish church) and browse the local market square. Pick up essentials at a local supermarket.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed welcome dinner in Lagoa town. Explore the pedestrian streets and enjoy a glass of local Algarve wine at a terrace café before an early night.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastel de nata and espresso at the airport or a café near the hotel upon arrival
meals.lunch: Light snack or sandwich at a local café in Lagoa after check-in (~€8–12)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Barradas or a similar local tasca in Lagoa — try cataplana de marisco (seafood stew) (~€18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light. Prioritize rest after travel. September in the Algarve is warm (~26–30°C) with minimal rain — ideal beach weather.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia de Carvoeiro, one of the most picturesque beaches near Lagoa (~10 min drive). Arrive early to claim a good spot. Swim, sunbathe, and explore the dramatic golden cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the Algar Seco coastal boardwalk (15 min from Carvoeiro) — a stunning network of pathways through sculpted rock formations and sea caves. Bring water and sunscreen.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Carvoeiro village. Browse the clifftop restaurants and enjoy sunset views over the Atlantic.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Lagoa Boutique Stay or a local café (~€6–10)
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish at a beach snack bar at Praia de Carvoeiro (~€12–16)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Castelo or similar in Carvoeiro — grilled sea bream or octopus salad (~€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Carvoeiro is very walkable. Parking can be tight in high season — consider arriving before 10am or taking a taxi/rideshare.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Silves (~15 min from Lagoa). Explore the magnificent red sandstone Silves Castle (Castelo de Silves), the best-preserved Moorish castle in the Algarve. Wander the ancient medina streets below.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museu Municipal de Arqueologia in Silves for context on the region's Moorish history. Then explore the riverside promenade along the Arade River and browse local artisan shops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa for dinner. Try a traditional Algarvian restaurant focusing on local specialties.

meals.breakfast: Café in Lagoa — toast with local honey and fresh orange juice (~€5–8)
meals.lunch: Lunch in Silves at Café Inglês (a local favorite near the castle) — piri piri chicken or grilled sardines (~€14–18)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Quatro Águas or similar in Lagoa — arroz de lingueirão (razor clam rice) (~€18–24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Silves Castle entry is approx €3–4. Wear comfortable shoes — the castle grounds involve uneven cobblestones. Silves hosts a Medieval Fair in August, but September is quieter and more pleasant.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting morning! Visit Adega do Cantor (Cliff Richard's winery) or Quinta dos Vales near Estômbar (~20 min from Lagoa). Take a guided cellar tour and taste local Algarve reds, whites, and rosés.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue wine exploration at a second nearby producer — Quinta da Penina or Adega Cooperativa do Algarve in Lagoa itself. Purchase a bottle or two to enjoy during the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Aperitivo evening in Lagoa — pair local cheeses, presunto (cured ham), and olives with your wine purchases at the hotel terrace or a local deli.

meals.lunch: Wine estate lunch (many estates offer cheese and charcuterie boards or light lunches) (~€15–20)
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at a tasca in Lagoa — bacalhau à brás (salt cod) or grilled pork with clams (~€16–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book winery tours in advance — Quinta dos Vales is particularly scenic with sculpture gardens. Algarve wines are underrated; the region produces excellent Negra Mole and Aragonez reds.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Praia da Marinha (~15 min from Lagoa), consistently ranked among Europe's most beautiful beaches. Explore the rock arches, sea caves, and crystal-clear water. Snorkeling is excellent here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the clifftop trail from Praia da Marinha toward Benagil (~45 min walk one way). Admire the dramatic coastal scenery and stop at Praia do Carvalho along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a cliffside bar near Carvoeiro, then dinner back in Lagoa.

meals.breakfast: Café in Lagoa — croissant, coffee, and fresh juice (~€5–8)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snack bar near Praia da Marinha — sandwiches and cold drinks (~€8–12)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Bon (Michelin-starred, splurge option) or a mid-range alternative in Carvoeiro (~€30–45 per person for Bon Bon; €18–25 elsewhere)

day_by_day.notes: Praia da Marinha has limited parking — arrive before 9:30am or take a taxi. The clifftop walk is moderately challenging; wear sturdy shoes. Bring plenty of water.

day_by_day.morning: Take a boat tour from Benagil (~20 min from Lagoa) to see the famous Benagil Sea Cave (Algar de Benagil) from the water — one of Portugal's most iconic natural wonders. Book in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the boat tour, relax at Praia de Benagil. In the late afternoon, drive to Portimão (~20 min) for a quick city exploration — stroll along the riverside promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Portimão — the city is famous for its sardine grilling culture, especially along the riverside.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or café in Lagoa (~€6–10)
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at a restaurant near Benagil beach (~€15–20)
meals.dinner: Tasca do Celso or similar riverside restaurant in Portimão — grilled sardines, espetada (meat skewers), and local wine (~€16–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Benagil boat tours sell out quickly — book 2–3 days ahead. Tours typically last 45–90 min and cost €15–25 per person. You cannot enter the cave on foot safely.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Lagos (~30 min from Lagoa). Explore the historic old town — walk the ancient city walls, visit Igreja de Santo António, and browse the colorful Praça Gil Eanes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Ponta da Piedade — a breathtaking series of golden rock formations and grottos just south of Lagos. Walk the clifftop paths and take optional kayak or paddleboard tours of the sea caves.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Lagos before returning to Lagoa. Lagos has an excellent restaurant scene.

meals.lunch: Lunch in Lagos old town — try A Forja or O Camilo for fresh seafood (~€16–22 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos — regional Algarvian cuisine with local wine (~€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is very popular — September is still busy but manageable. Ponta da Piedade is best visited in the afternoon when the light is golden. Kayak tours cost ~€20–30 per person.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning at Praia de Armação de Pêra (~20 min from Lagoa) — a long, wide sandy beach perfect for a relaxed swim and morning walk along the shore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Nossa Senhora da Rocha chapel perched dramatically on a promontory between two beaches. Then explore the village of Armação de Pêra and its small fishing harbor.
day_by_day.evening: Back in Lagoa — wine and tapas evening at a local wine bar, sampling more Algarve and Alentejo wines.

meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at a restaurant on Armação de Pêra beachfront — grilled sea bass or ameijoas à bulhão pato (clams) (~€14–20)
meals.dinner: Wine bar dinner in Lagoa — sharing plates of local cheeses, smoked sausages, and pataniscas de bacalhau (cod fritters) (~€15–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Armação de Pêra has one of the longest beaches in the Algarve. The Nossa Senhora da Rocha chapel is free to visit and offers stunning views.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Monchique (~45 min from Lagoa) in the Algarve's inland mountains. Hike or drive to the summit of Fóia — the highest point in the Algarve — for panoramic views stretching to the Atlantic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming mountain village of Monchique — browse artisan shops selling local medronho (arbutus berry brandy) and honey. Visit the ruined Franciscan convent.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa. Dinner featuring inland Algarve cuisine — hearty mountain flavors as a contrast to the coastal diet.

meals.lunch: Traditional lunch in Monchique at Restaurante Central or similar — roast lamb or pork with migas (~€14–18 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Lagoa — try bifanas (pork sandwiches) or a full carne de porco à alentejana (pork with clams) (~€16–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Monchique is noticeably cooler than the coast — bring a light layer. The medronho brandy is a local specialty worth tasting (responsibly!). Roads to Fóia summit are narrow but paved.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the coast for a morning at Praia da Galé (~15 min from Lagoa) — a beautiful, less crowded beach with golden sand and calm waters. Perfect for swimming and relaxation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Albufeira (~25 min from Lagoa) — explore the historic old town (away from the tourist strip), the fishing harbor, and the clifftop views. Browse the local market.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Albufeira old town — pick a restaurant with a terrace and enjoy the lively evening atmosphere.

meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Praia da Galé — toasted sandwiches, salads, and cold drinks (~€10–14)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Ruína in Albufeira (iconic clifftop location) or similar — fresh grilled fish and local wine (~€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Albufeira can be very touristy in the main strip — stick to the old town for a more authentic experience. Praia da Galé is quieter than Albufeira's main beaches.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated wine tasting day — visit Adega Cooperativa do Algarve in Lagoa for a deeper dive into local winemaking. Take a tour of the production facilities and taste their award-winning wines.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Alentejo border region (~1 hr) to visit Herdade dos Pinheiros or a similar estate winery for a contrasting wine experience. The Alentejo is one of Portugal's premier wine regions.
day_by_day.evening: Wine pairing dinner back in Lagoa — choose a restaurant that offers a curated wine list to complement the day's discoveries.

meals.breakfast: Café in Lagoa — fresh pastries and coffee (~€5–8)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the winery or a picnic with local bread, cheese, and charcuterie purchased from a local deli (~€12–16)
meals.dinner: Elegant dinner at a Lagoa restaurant with wine pairing — grilled turbot or black pork medallions with regional wine (~€28–38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Adega Cooperativa do Algarve in Lagoa is one of the region's oldest and most respected wine producers. Call ahead to arrange tours. Designated driver or rideshare strongly recommended for this day.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach morning at Praia dos Três Irmãos (~20 min from Lagoa) near Alvor — a stunning beach with sea caves, rock arches, and calm turquoise water. Take a leisurely swim and soak in the scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the charming fishing village of Alvor — stroll the wooden boardwalks over the Alvor estuary (Ria de Alvor), spot flamingos and wading birds, and explore the pretty whitewashed village center.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — celebrate the trip with a special meal. Choose one of the Algarve's finest restaurants for a memorable last evening.

meals.lunch: Seafood lunch in Alvor village — percebes (barnacles), fresh prawns, or cataplana (~€18–25 per person)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a top Lagoa/Carvoeiro restaurant — splurge on a tasting menu or a special seafood platter with premium local wine (~€35–50 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Alvor estuary is a protected nature reserve — excellent for birdwatching, especially in September when migratory birds pass through. Bring binoculars if you have them.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning — enjoy a long breakfast at the hotel, pack, and take a slow walk around Lagoa town one last time. Visit any shops for last-minute souvenirs (local wine, carob products, handmade ceramics).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Lagoa Boutique Stay. Transfer to Faro Airport (~35 min). Allow extra time for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry wonderful Algarve memories (and a bottle of local wine in your checked luggage!) back home.

meals.breakfast: Final full breakfast at hotel or a beloved local café (~€8–12)
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Lagoa before departure or at Faro Airport (~€10–15)
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Faro Airport is small but can get busy — arrive at least 2 hours before departure. Check luggage allowances if purchasing wine bottles to take home. September flights are still popular, so confirm transfer timing the night before.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Faro Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from Faro Airport to Lagoa Boutique Stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Lagoa Boutique Stay. Check-in, settle into your suite, and enjoy a welcome drink and orientation with your personal concierge. Take a leisurely stroll around the charming town of Lagoa to orient yourself.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the hotel's terrace or pool area as the sun sets over the Algarve. Light introduction to the region over a curated welcome aperitif arranged by the hotel.

meals.lunch: Light snack or refreshments upon arrival at the hotel — charcuterie board, local cheeses, and sparkling wine prepared by the hotel
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante O Barradas (Silves area) — one of the Algarve's most celebrated fine-dining institutions, known for traditional Portuguese cuisine elevated with modern technique. Reservations essential.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Ask the concierge to prepare a welcome amenity and a briefing pack for the full itinerary. Confirm dinner reservation before arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the hotel followed by a private guided visit to the medieval hilltop town of Silves — explore the impressive Moorish castle (Castelo de Silves), the Gothic cathedral, and the charming cobbled streets. Silves is only 10 minutes from Lagoa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private wine tasting experience at Quinta dos Vales, one of the Algarve's most prestigious wine estates near Lagoa. Tour the vineyards, cellar, and sculpture garden, followed by a guided tasting of their premium red, white, and rosé wines paired with local charcuterie and artisan cheeses.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails on the hotel terrace followed by a refined dinner in Lagoa town.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the hotel — freshly baked pastries, local fruit, eggs to order, smoked fish, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Wine estate picnic-style lunch included in the Quinta dos Vales tasting experience — local bread, cured meats, regional cheeses, and estate wines
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Bon Bon (Carvoeiro) — a Michelin-starred restaurant just minutes from Lagoa, offering an exceptional tasting menu celebrating Algarve ingredients with creative flair

day_by_day.notes: Book Quinta dos Vales private tasting in advance. Bon Bon is Michelin-starred — reservations should be made weeks ahead. Dress smart-casual for dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Private boat charter from Carvoeiro Marina (10 minutes from hotel) for a morning cruise along the stunning Algarve coastline — explore the iconic sea caves, grottoes, and golden cliffs of Benagil and surroundings. Swim in secluded coves accessible only by boat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the legendary Praia de Benagil beach and the famous Benagil Sea Cave from the water. Anchor in a private cove for a gourmet lunch served on board. Snorkeling equipment provided.
day_by_day.evening: Return to hotel for a relaxing spa treatment (arrange with concierge). Freshen up for a sunset dinner.

meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch served on the private boat — fresh seafood, local wines, artisan bread, and seasonal Algarve produce
meals.dinner: Dinner at A Ver Tavira (Carvoeiro cliff-top restaurant) — exceptional views of the Atlantic with a menu focused on fresh Algarve seafood and Portuguese classics

day_by_day.notes: Full-day private boat charter should be booked well in advance, especially for September. Bring sunscreen, hats, and swimwear. September waters are still warm and ideal for swimming.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Algarve's wine country — visit Adega do Cantor (the winery associated with Cliff Richard) near Guia, just 20 minutes from Lagoa. Explore the estate, learn about the unique Algarve terroir, and enjoy a premium tasting of their award-winning wines.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the spectacular Praia da Marinha — consistently rated one of Europe's most beautiful beaches, located just 15 minutes from Lagoa. Arrange a private sunbed and parasol setup through the hotel concierge. Swim in the crystal-clear turquoise waters surrounded by dramatic golden limestone cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to hotel for a private in-room or terrace dining experience — the hotel arranges a chef's table or curated room service with a sommelier-selected wine pairing.

meals.lunch: Light seafood lunch at the beach restaurant at Praia da Marinha or a gourmet beach picnic prepared by the hotel
meals.dinner: Private chef's table dinner at the hotel — a bespoke multi-course tasting menu with Algarve-sourced ingredients and premium Portuguese wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Praia da Marinha requires a short walk down steps — wear comfortable footwear. The private chef's table dinner should be arranged with the hotel concierge 24–48 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private helicopter tour over the Algarve coastline — depart from a nearby helipad for a breathtaking aerial perspective of the golden cliffs, hidden beaches, and sea caves stretching from Lagos to Faro. Approximately 45–60 minutes in the air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the historic town of Lagos — explore the old town walls, the Igreja de Santo António (a stunning baroque church), the Slave Market Museum, and the vibrant Praça Gil Eanes. Browse high-end local boutiques and artisan shops.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a clifftop bar in Lagos followed by dinner at one of the town's finest restaurants.

meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Villas Lagos — elegant setting with garden views and a menu of refined Portuguese and Mediterranean cuisine
meals.dinner: Dinner at No Pátio (Lagos) — intimate fine-dining restaurant in a beautiful courtyard setting, celebrated for its creative Portuguese tasting menu and exceptional wine list

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter tours must be booked well in advance and are weather-dependent. Lagos is approximately 30 minutes from Lagoa by private car. Arrange private transfer for the day.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga or wellness session arranged at the hotel (private instructor). Followed by a leisurely breakfast and a visit to the Lagoa Municipal Market to explore local produce, fresh fish, and artisan goods — a wonderful insight into authentic Algarve daily life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided visit to the Algar Seco rock formations in Carvoeiro — a dramatic landscape of sculpted limestone cliffs, arches, and sea pools. Walk the clifftop paths and enjoy the extraordinary geological scenery. Followed by time at Praia de Carvoeiro beach.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive wine dinner experience — the hotel concierge arranges a private sommelier-led dinner featuring a curated selection of premium Portuguese wines (Douro, Alentejo, Algarve) paired with a five-course tasting menu.

meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante O Castelo (Carvoeiro) — panoramic clifftop views and a menu of fresh Algarve seafood and grilled fish
meals.dinner: Private sommelier-led wine dinner at the hotel — five-course tasting menu with premium Portuguese wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Algar Seco is a short walk from Carvoeiro beach. Wear sturdy footwear for the rocky paths. The private wine dinner should be arranged with the hotel at least 48 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente — the southwestern-most point of continental Europe. Visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres (Sagres Fortress) and stand at the windswept cliff edge of Cabo de São Vicente, a place of immense historical and natural grandeur. Private guided tour with a historian.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the wild and unspoiled beaches of the Costa Vicentina near Sagres — Praia do Beliche or Praia da Mareta. These Atlantic-facing beaches have a raw, dramatic beauty distinct from the sheltered southern coast. Swim or simply enjoy the powerful scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa. Dinner at a celebrated local restaurant.

meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Memmo Baleeira (Sagres) — a stylish hotel restaurant with panoramic ocean views and a menu celebrating local Atlantic seafood
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Sueste (Ferragudo) — an intimate riverside restaurant in the picturesque fishing village of Ferragudo (15 minutes from Lagoa), renowned for its exceptional fresh fish and cataplana dishes

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is approximately 60–70 minutes from Lagoa by private car. Start the day early to maximize time. The private historian guide should be arranged through the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private stand-up paddleboarding or kayaking session along the calm waters near Ferragudo and the Arade River estuary — a serene and beautiful morning on the water with views of Ferragudo village and Portimão beyond. Guided by a private instructor.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the charming fishing village of Ferragudo — wander the whitewashed streets, visit the 16th-century Castelo de São João do Arade, and browse the artisan galleries. Followed by a leisurely afternoon at Praia de Ferragudo, one of the Algarve's most beautiful and less-crowded beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitivo on the terrace of the hotel followed by a relaxed but refined dinner.

meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante A Tasca (Ferragudo) — a beloved local gem serving outstanding grilled fish, seafood rice, and traditional petiscos in a charming village setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Água Mole (Portimão) — contemporary Portuguese cuisine with an emphasis on local seafood and regional wines

day_by_day.notes: Ferragudo is just 10 minutes from Lagoa. The SUP/kayaking session should be booked through a premium water sports provider. September waters are warm and calm — ideal conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided wine tour of the interior Algarve — visit the lesser-known but highly regarded wineries of the Serra de Monchique foothills. Explore Quinta da Penina or similar boutique estates, learning about indigenous grape varieties like Negra Mole and Crato Branco.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue into the Serra de Monchique mountain range — visit the spa town of Caldas de Monchique, a historic thermal resort nestled in lush eucalyptus and cork oak forests. Enjoy a thermal spa session or a walk through the beautiful gardens. Visit the hilltop village of Monchique for panoramic views over the Algarve.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa. Relax and enjoy a quiet evening at the hotel.

meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Luar da Foia (Monchique) — a charming mountain restaurant with spectacular views and a menu of hearty Algarve mountain cuisine, including roast lamb and local presunto
meals.dinner: Dinner at the hotel — request a private terrace dinner under the stars with a curated menu and wine selection arranged by the concierge

day_by_day.notes: Monchique is approximately 40 minutes from Lagoa. The mountain roads are winding — a private driver is recommended. The thermal spa in Caldas de Monchique should be booked in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise beach experience at Praia de Carvoeiro — the hotel arranges a private setup with champagne, fresh fruit, and pastries for a magical early morning on the beach as the sun rises over the Atlantic. Followed by a morning swim.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Portimão Museum (Museu de Portimão) — an award-winning museum housed in a converted 19th-century fish canning factory, offering a fascinating insight into the history and culture of the Algarve. Followed by a luxury shopping experience in Portimão's boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-style grand dinner at one of the Algarve's finest establishments.

meals.breakfast: Private sunrise champagne breakfast on the beach at Praia de Carvoeiro
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Titanic (Portimão) — a long-established Portimão institution celebrated for its exceptional fresh fish and traditional Algarve seafood dishes
meals.dinner: Return dinner at Restaurante Bon Bon (Carvoeiro) — revisit the Michelin-starred experience with a different tasting menu selection, celebrating the finest Algarve produce

day_by_day.notes: The sunrise beach setup must be arranged with the hotel concierge the evening before. Portimão is 15 minutes from Lagoa. Bon Bon reservations must be made well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided jeep safari through the Algarve's stunning interior — explore hidden cork oak forests, ancient Roman ruins, and traditional whitewashed villages in the backcountry between Lagoa and Silves. A unique perspective on the authentic Algarve far from the coast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Silves Wine Festival area (if seasonal events are running) or return to Quinta dos Vales for a private blending workshop — create your own personalized bottle of Algarve wine under the guidance of the estate's head winemaker.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the hotel with a premium in-room spa treatment followed by dinner.

meals.lunch: Rustic farmhouse lunch arranged as part of the jeep safari — traditional Algarve dishes including cataplana de marisco, local bread, and regional wines served in a countryside setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante O Barradas (Silves) — return visit to this celebrated restaurant for a final exploration of their seasonal tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: The jeep safari should be booked through a premium tour operator. The wine blending workshop at Quinta dos Vales must be arranged in advance and is a truly unique luxury experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning of leisure — a slow, indulgent breakfast at the hotel followed by a private yoga or meditation session in the hotel garden. Spend time reflecting on the journey and enjoying the tranquil Lagoa surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final beach afternoon at Praia de Carvoeiro or Praia da Marinha — the hotel arranges a premium beach setup with sunbeds, parasol, chilled towels, and a cooler of drinks and snacks. Swim, read, and soak up the last of the Algarve sun.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner — a special occasion meal at the finest available restaurant, celebrating the end of a magnificent journey through the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Extended gourmet farewell breakfast at the hotel — the full spread with champagne, smoked salmon, local pastries, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Light beach lunch — fresh seafood, salads, and chilled rosé wine arranged by the hotel
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at Restaurante Bon Bon or a private chef experience at the hotel — multi-course tasting menu with the hotel sommelier's finest wine pairings, ending with a dessert wine and petit fours

day_by_day.notes: Arrange any final souvenirs or gifts through the hotel concierge — local wines, artisan ceramics, or gourmet food products make excellent mementos. Pack the evening before departure.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Algarve. Leisurely last breakfast at the hotel. Check out and arrange private luxury transfer to Faro Airport for departure. Allow ample time for the 45-minute transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Faro Airport. Carry the memories of 13 extraordinary days in the Algarve.
day_by_day.evening: In transit or arrived at destination.

meals.breakfast: Final gourmet breakfast at the hotel before checkout
meals.lunch: Light refreshments at Faro Airport or on board
meals.dinner: In transit

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private luxury transfer to Faro Airport well in advance. Allow at least 2 hours before flight departure. The concierge can arrange a farewell gift or a bottle of Algarve wine to take home. Confirm all transfers and any final hotel charges the evening before.
